. This is the canonical agent for confirming your code is safe before shipping.
- ci: Poll CI status, logs, and failures for the current branch; run specific steps locally in a container for diagnosis.
- git-tricks: Git troubleshooting — unstage, reset, abort rebase, undo a commit, fix push-to-wrong-branch, get the branch name you meant to switch to, find the commit that broke X, and more. Don't read the git manual yourself. (Tools: Bash, LSP)
- git-workflow: Use for multi-commit/multi-branch workflows and to create pull requests; also for authoring, amending, force-pushing, or rebasing commits. When the user asks "how do I...", "I made a mistake with my commits", "how to rearrange commits", "push to a new branch", "rebase / squash / reorder commits", or asks for help with a merge conflict. (Tools: Bash, Read, Edit, Write, LSP)
- git-flow: Coordinate branch / PR / release / track updates workflows; for multi-person coordination, pull-request governance, hotfix chains, release automation. (Tools: Bash, LSP)
- code-golf: Code transformation mini-language to rewrite large swaths of code at once. Use when: code spans multiple different files or >100 lines per file; the rewrite is structural (reorder / retemplate / unify variable names / generalize); OR when similar code appears in 5+ places and the user wants to consolidate. Not for: inline edits (use Edit), single-file refactors (use Edit), or code review (use /code-review). Prompt format: describe the transformation in prose or pseudocode; the agent encodes it as rules and applies them. (Tools: Read, Edit, Bash, LSP)
- git-mass-refactor: Large-scale cross-repo refactoring and mass migrations. Use to refactor hundreds of lines / dozens of files / multiple repos at once. For single-repo refactoring, /code-golf is faster. (Tools: Agent, Bash, Read, Edit, Write, LSP)
- docker: Debug Docker builds and container configuration, run containers locally, and trace image/layer structure. (Tools: Bash, Read, Edit, Write)
- packing: Packaging-infra-only hardening for `deb` / `rpm` / `dmg` / `AppImage` / `snap` / `nix` — configuration files, maintainer scripts (preinst/postinst/prerm/postrm), GPG signing, dependency declarations. Use when working on packaging logic (not the artifact contents). Do NOT use for CMake/Gradle/cargo — use language-specific build tools instead. (Tools: Read, Edit, Write, Bash, LSP)
- build: Diagnose and fix build issues. Use when a build fails, tests fail, or you need to run a complex build locally. (Tools: Bash, Read, Edit, LSP)
- migrate: Dependency upgrade troubleshooting — understand what broke and fix forward (not pin to an older version). Use when upgrading npm/maven/gradle/pip/cargo/gem/go/other-pkg-mgr dependencies or major SemVer bumps. (Tools: Bash, Read, Edit, Write, LSP)
- test: Run tests, interpret results, and debug failures. Use this when you need to verify, debug, or expand test coverage. Can parse test output (pytest/jest/vitest/mocha/gtest/JUnit), pinpoint failures, and do root-cause analysis. (Tools: Bash, Read, Edit, Write, LSP)
- codemod: Run codemods / AST-based transformations to rewrite code in bulk. Used for linting fixes, API upgrades, and structural refactors. (Tools: Bash, Read, Edit, Write, LSP)
- storybook: Set up, debug, and extend Storybook. Use when working on a Storybook config or story file. Includes Storybook-specific test runners, diagnostics, controls, and shortcuts. (Tools: Read, Edit, Write, Bash, LSP)
- nodejs: Node.js / npm / pnpm version upgrade; project setup; runtime issue diagnosis. (Tools: Bash, Read, Edit, Write, LSP)
- frontend: Diagnose and fix frontend issues — runtime errors, build config bugs, browser compatibility, missing styles, flaky E2E tests. (Tools: Bash, Read, Edit, Write, LSP)
- python: Set up Python environments, manage dependencies, fix compatibility issues, and diagnose runtime errors. (Tools: Bash, Read, Edit, Write, LSP)
